legend: There is a binary tree of n+1%%ZSMJ0%% vertices (n%%ZSMJ1%% is odd), with vertices labeled 0,1,…,n%%ZSMJ2%%. At most one letter can be written on each vertex of the tree, and all vertices initially have nothing written on them. The root of the tree is vertex 0%%ZSMJ3%%.
In the tree, vertex 0%%ZSMJ4%% is the parent of vertex 1%%ZSMJ5%%, while all other vertices have either 2%%ZSMJ6%% children or 0%%ZSMJ7%% children.

Bob is lost in one vertex of the tree and wishes to escape the tree by reaching vertex 0%%ZSMJ8%%. This is very easy for most people with common sense. However, since Bob is an idiot, he created a new way of traversing the tree; introducing the "Idiot First Search".
When Bob is on vertex v%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤v≤n%%ZSMJ10%%), Bob's movement is determined as follows:
If vertex v%%ZSMJ11%% is a leaf, Bob always moves to the parent of v%%ZSMJ12%%; otherwise, check the next few conditions.
If nothing is written on vertex v%%ZSMJ13%%, Bob writes 'L' on vertex v%%ZSMJ14%% and moves to the left child of v%%ZSMJ15%%;
If 'L' is written on vertex v%%ZSMJ16%%, Bob overwrites it to 'R' and moves to the right child of v%%ZSMJ17%%;
If 'R' is written on vertex v%%ZSMJ18%%, Bob erases it and moves to the parent of v%%ZSMJ19%%.
It takes exactly 1%%ZSMJ20%% second for Bob to move to an adjacent vertex, so Bob will take exactly x%%ZSMJ21%% seconds to perform x%%ZSMJ22%% moves.

It has been shown that regardless of which vertex Bob starts on, Bob can reach vertex 0%%ZSMJ23%% in a finite (though possibly inexplicably large) amount of time. We don't know who proved it; surely it can't be Bob, but it is definitely proven.

For each vertex k=1,2,…,n%%ZSMJ24%%, please determine the total time it takes to reach vertex 0%%ZSMJ25%% if Bob started on vertex k%%ZSMJ26%%, in seconds. As the values may be huge, you are only asked to compute them modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ27%%.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ29%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤n≤300001%%ZSMJ31%%, n%%ZSMJ32%% is odd).
Each of the next n%%ZSMJ33%% lines contains two integers li%%ZSMJ34%% and ri%%ZSMJ35%% denoting the children of vertex i%%ZSMJ36%% (0≤li,ri≤n%%ZSMJ37%%).
For each vertex, li=ri=0%%ZSMJ38%% is given if the vertex has no children. Otherwise, li%%ZSMJ39%% and ri%%ZSMJ40%% are the left and right children of vertex i%%ZSMJ41%%.
It is guaranteed that the input defines a valid binary tree satisfying the conditions given in the statement.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ42%% over all test cases does not exceed 300001%%ZSMJ43%%.
output: For each test case, output n%%ZSMJ44%% integers τ1,τ2,…,τn%%ZSMJ45%% separated by spaces.
Here, τk%%ZSMJ46%% denotes the total time it takes to reach vertex 0%%ZSMJ47%% if Bob started on vertex k%%ZSMJ48%%, modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ49%%.
note: On the first test case, there are only two vertices, vertex 0%%ZSMJ50%% and vertex 1%%ZSMJ51%%. It takes only 1%%ZSMJ52%% second for Bob to reach vertex 0%%ZSMJ53%% from vertex 1%%ZSMJ54%%.
